entries.english:
1292, 3 July, Prague. — King Wenceslas II gives Hohenfurt Abbey eight villages in exchange for the villages of Zdradonicz, Malschitz, and Zaborsi, including Stricitz with its church, and part of the forest by Dobschitz. In 1292, date unspecified, at Rome, several archbishops and bishops grant indulgences to the church of the Blessed Virgin Mary at Hohenfurt.

We, Wenceslas, by the grace of God King of Bohemia, Duke of Kraków and Sandomierz, and Margrave of Moravia, wish by this instrument to make known to all, present and future, that the late Lord Otakar, illustrious King of Bohemia and our dearest father, took the market village called Zdradonicz near our city of Budweis, as well as Plawen, Malschitz, and Zaborsi, which belonged to the Cistercian monastery at Hohenfurt. He attached three of these, namely Zdradonicz, Malschitz, and Zaborsi, to that city. In exchange for these four villages, our aforesaid father assigned to the said monastery the villages called Nencitz, Bellecia, Craschan, and Tupes, formerly belonging to Zuatumir, knight of Nemcicz. Since the heirs of that knight have fully proved to us that these same villages—Nemchicz, Bellela, Craschau, and Tupes—rightfully belonged to them, we have decided to restore them to those heirs.

Therefore, wishing to keep the monastery harmless with respect to the aforesaid exchange, we restore the aforesaid village of Plawen to the monastery. In exchange for the aforesaid three villages, Zdradonicz, Malschicz, and Zaborsi, we give, transfer, and assign to the monastery at Hohenfurt our villages called Strishicz, with the church situated there, Borach, Zaborsi, Badiczi, Holaschawicz, Shemil, Dubshicz, and Lupanawicz, as well as part of the Chraski forest up to the boundaries between the lands of the monastery of the Holy Crown and those of Heinrich von Rosenberg and Johann von Monte Michaelis. We grant these with their meadows, pastures, cultivated and uncultivated fields, waters and watercourses, fishing, hunting, and all rights, claims, and appurtenances belonging to those villages. The abbot and convent of Hohenfurt are to possess them in perpetuity under the title of exchange. In testimony, we have ordered these present letters to be drawn up and secured by the protection of our seals.

Given at Prague through the hand of our master Peter, our protonotary and canon of the churches of Prague, Wrocław, and Vyšehrad, in the year of the Lord 1292, on 3 July, indiction 5.

Seal: Damaged, like the seal described in no. XXXVIII. Millauer, p. 110, no. 26.

XLVI. 1292, date unspecified, Rome. — Several archbishops and bishops grant indulgences to the church of the Blessed Virgin Mary at Hohenfurt.

To all the faithful of Christ who inspect these present letters: Roger, Archbishop of Sezze, and John, Archbishop of Muc, by the grace of God; Cyprian of Vov, James of Acerra, Salvo of Racanati, Daniel of Lacedonia, Perronus of Larino, James of Trivento, William of Cagli, Romanus of Crotone, and Berard of Foligno, bishops by the same grace, send everlasting greetings in the Lord. The glory of eternal life, by which the wondrous goodness of the Creator of all crowns the blessed assembly of the citizens of heaven, must be attained by the redeemed through the merit of the blood poured from the precious body of the Redeemer. Among the means to this end, it is known to be especially important that the majesty of the Most High be praised everywhere, and above all in the churches of the saints.

Wishing that the church of Saint Mary the Virgin at Hohenfurt, belonging to the religious men of the Cistercian Order in the Diocese of Prague, be frequented with due honor and continually venerated by all the faithful of Christ—and since that church is being built at great expense and does not have sufficient resources of its own to bring this praiseworthy work, begun in Mary’s honor, to a worthy completion—we admonish, ask, and exhort you in the Lord to give pious alms and welcome charitable assistance from the goods God has given you, for the construction of that church and the remission of your sins.

Trusting in the mercy of almighty God and in the authority of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul, we mercifully grant in the Lord forty days’ remission of the penances imposed on each of all those who are truly penitent and have confessed, provided the diocesan bishop consents: those who extend helping hands toward the construction of the aforesaid church; those who visit it devotionally on the feasts of the Nativity of the Lord, the Resurrection, the Ascension, and Pentecost; on the four feasts of the glorious Virgin Mary; on the feasts of Michael the Archangel, John the Baptist, John the Evangelist, Peter and Paul and the other apostles, Lawrence the martyr, Martin and Nicholas the confessors, and Mary Magdalene, Catherine, Margaret, and Cecilia the virgins; on All Saints’ Day; on the day of the church’s dedication or its anniversary; and on every Friday throughout the year; or those who, when near death, bequeath any of their means to the aforesaid church. In testimony, we have caused this present document to be authenticated by the protection of our seals.

Given at Rome in the year of the Lord 1292, in the fifth year of the pontificate of Pope Nicholas IV.

Seals: Eleven seals, more or less well preserved, in red wax hanging from red silk threads. The first two show a seated bishop blessing; their surviving legends identify Roger, Archbishop of Sezze, and John, Archbishop of Muc. Several others show a blessing bishop. One shows the Virgin Mary above a kneeling bishop, with a heraldic lily at the right and a horned animal’s head at the left. Another shows the Virgin Mary above a kneeling bishop. One shows a standing blessing bishop with an angel blessing him from above; its legend identifies Berard, Bishop of Foligno.

XLVII. 1292, date unspecified, Rome. — Several bishops grant indulgences to the church of Saint Nicholas at Rosenberg.

To all the faithful of Christ to whom these present letters come: John, by the grace of God Archbishop of Muc, Cyprian of Vov, Perronus of Larino, Brother Daniel of Lacedonia, James of Trivento, William of Cagli, and Romanus of Crotone, bishops by the same grace, send everlasting greetings in the Lord. The glory of eternal life, by which the wondrous goodness of the Creator of all crowns the blessed assembly of the citizens of heaven, must be attained by the redeemed through the merit of the blood poured from the precious body of the Redeemer. Among the means to this end, it is known to be especially important that the majesty of the Most High be praised everywhere, and particularly in the churches of the saints.

Wishing that the parish church of Saint Nicholas the Confessor at Rosenberg in the Diocese of Prague be frequented with due honor and continually venerated by all the faithful of Christ, we grant to all who are truly penitent and have confessed forty days’ remission of the penances imposed on each of them, provided the diocesan bishop consents. This applies to those who visit that church devotionally on the feasts listed here: the Nativity of the Lord, the Resurrection, the Ascension, and Pentecost; the four feasts of the blessed and glorious ever-Virgin Mary; the feasts of Michael the Archangel, John the Baptist, John the Evangelist, Peter and Paul, Nicholas the bishop, Mary Magdalene, Margaret, and Catherine the virgins, and the other patrons of that church; the day of its dedication or the anniversary of that day; and throughout the octaves of the aforesaid feasts. It also applies to those who extend helping hands toward the construction of the church, its lamps, ornaments, or other needs, and to those who, when near death, bequeath any of their means to the aforesaid church. In testimony, we have caused this present document to be authenticated by the protection of our seals.

Given at Rome in the year of the Lord 1292, while the Apostolic See was vacant.

Seals: Six seals, hanging from red silk threads, very badly damaged. Five correspond to seals described under no. XLVI; the sixth is entirely missing.

XLVIII. 1293, 25 February, Rosenberg. — Heinrich von Rosenberg grants his servant Ulrich, called Gusner, the village of Waldau as free hereditary property in reward for his faithful service.

When a deed is committed to writing, every opportunity for dispute is forestalled. Therefore, we, Heinrich, lord of Rosenberg, make known to all, present and future, that, considering the loyalty of the service of our faithful servant Ulrich called Gusner, we have granted him our village of Waldau, with everything rightfully belonging to it—namely its fields, meadows, and forests—to possess by hereditary right. In testimony and as the strongest confirmation of this grant, we have caused this present letter to be secured by the protection of our seal.

The witnesses listed below are: Lord Wenceslas, burgrave at Rosenberg; Wolfrad of Gusen; Zenco of Zipin and Dworata, his son; Ulrich of Weichsel; Pribislaus Lednicer; Ortlin Seubelberger; Freisinger; Ditmar of Nemze; Ulrich of Sestau; Walwan; Peter; Otto; Troian; Zastawoi; and many other trustworthy people.

Done and given at Rosenberg in the year of the Lord 1293, on 25 February.

Seal: Heinrich von Rosenberg’s well-preserved equestrian seal, hanging from violet and yellow-red silk. Compare no. XXXIII.
